questions.q:
Compound 'P' is formed by the oxidation of cumene followed by acidic hydrolysis. 'P' undergoes three separate reactions as follows:
(i) 'P' reacts with Reagent I to give $p$-benzoquinone.
(ii) 'P' reacts with Reagent II to give a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol.
(iii) 'P' reacts with Reagent III to give $p$-bromophenol as the major product.

Identify Reagent I, Reagent II, and Reagent III.
questions.question:
Compound 'P' is formed by the oxidation of cumene followed by acidic hydrolysis. 'P' undergoes three separate reactions as follows:
(i) 'P' reacts with Reagent I to give $p$-benzoquinone.
(ii) 'P' reacts with Reagent II to give a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol.
(iii) 'P' reacts with Reagent III to give $p$-bromophenol as the major product.

Identify Reagent I, Reagent II, and Reagent III.
questions.solution:
The oxidation of cumene followed by acidic hydrolysis is the commercial method for the preparation of phenol. Thus, compound 'P' is phenol.

Reaction (i): Phenol undergoes oxidation with a strong oxidizing agent like acidified sodium dichromate ($\text{Na}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 / \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$) to produce a conjugated diketone known as $p$-benzoquinone. Hence, Reagent I is $\text{Na}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 / \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.

Reaction (ii): When phenol is treated with bromine water ($\text{Br}_2$ in a polar solvent like $\text{H}_2\text{O}$), the highly activating nature of the $-\text{OH}$ group causes polyhalogenation, yielding a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol. Hence, Reagent II is $\text{Br}_2$ in $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

Reaction (iii): When phenol is treated with bromine in a non-polar solvent such as $\text{CS}_2$ or $\text{CHCl}_3$ at low temperature, monobromination occurs, giving $p$-bromophenol as the major product. Hence, Reagent III is $\text{Br}_2$ in $\text{CS}_2$.

Answer: I: $\text{Na}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 / \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, II: $\text{Br}_2$ in $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, III: $\text{Br}_2$ in $\text{CS}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider cyclohexanol as the reference molecule for acid-catalyzed dehydration. Among the following compounds, how many will undergo acid-catalyzed dehydration at a faster rate than cyclohexanol?
(i) 1-Methylcyclohexan-1-ol
(ii) Cyclohexa-2,4-dien-1-ol
(iii) Cyclohex-2-en-1-ol
(iv) 1-Phenylethan-1-ol
(v) Cyclohexylmethanol
(vi) Phenol
questions.question:
Consider cyclohexanol as the reference molecule for acid-catalyzed dehydration. Among the following compounds, how many will undergo acid-catalyzed dehydration at a faster rate than cyclohexanol?
(i) 1-Methylcyclohexan-1-ol
(ii) Cyclohexa-2,4-dien-1-ol
(iii) Cyclohex-2-en-1-ol
(iv) 1-Phenylethan-1-ol
(v) Cyclohexylmethanol
(vi) Phenol
questions.solution:
The rate of acid-catalyzed dehydration of an alcohol is directly proportional to the stability of the intermediate carbocation formed.

Cyclohexanol dehydrates via a secondary carbocation (cyclohexyl cation). Let us evaluate the intermediate carbocations for the given compounds:

(i) 1-Methylcyclohexan-1-ol forms a tertiary carbocation, which is more stable than a secondary carbocation. (Faster)

(ii) Cyclohexa-2,4-dien-1-ol forms a resonance-stabilized dienyl cation and loses a proton to form the highly stable aromatic ring (benzene). (Faster)

(iii) Cyclohex-2-en-1-ol forms an allylic carbocation, which is stabilized by resonance and is more stable than a simple secondary carbocation. (Faster)

(iv) 1-Phenylethan-1-ol forms a benzylic carbocation, which is highly stabilized by resonance with the benzene ring. (Faster)

(v) Cyclohexylmethanol forms a primary carbocation, which is less stable than a secondary carbocation. (Slower)

(vi) Phenol does not undergo acid-catalyzed dehydration because the C-O bond is stronger due to partial double bond character, and the phenyl cation is highly unstable. (Slower)

Thus, $4$ compounds undergo dehydration faster than cyclohexanol.

Answer: $4$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : The boiling point of n-butyl alcohol is higher than that of tert-butyl alcohol, but both have higher boiling points than diethyl ether.

Reason (R) : Boiling points of alcohols decrease with an increase in branching due to a decrease in surface area, while alcohols have higher boiling points than isomeric ethers due to the presence of intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
questions.question:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : The boiling point of n-butyl alcohol is higher than that of tert-butyl alcohol, but both have higher boiling points than diethyl ether.

Reason (R) : Boiling points of alcohols decrease with an increase in branching due to a decrease in surface area, while alcohols have higher boiling points than isomeric ethers due to the presence of intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct. n-butyl alcohol is a straight-chain alcohol and tert-butyl alcohol is its branched isomer. Both are alcohols and have higher boiling points than diethyl ether, which is an ether of comparable molecular mass.

Reason (R) is also correct and provides the exact physical explanation for the Assertion. For isomeric alcohols, as branching increases, the molecule becomes more spherical, which decreases the surface area and consequently weakens the van der Waals forces. This explains why n-butyl alcohol has a higher boiling point than tert-butyl alcohol. Furthermore, alcohols possess the ability to form intermolecular hydrogen bonds, requiring more energy to separate the molecules compared to the weak dipole-dipole interactions present in ethers like diethyl ether. This explains why both alcohols boil at higher temperatures than diethyl ether.

Thus, both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The cyclic alcohol 1-phenylcyclopentan-1-ol is synthesized by reacting a di-Grignard reagent, prepared from a dihalide 'X', with an ester 'Y', followed by acidic hydrolysis. Identify the correct pair of starting materials 'X' and 'Y'.
questions.question: The cyclic alcohol 1-phenylcyclopentan-1-ol is synthesized by reacting a di-Grignard reagent, prepared from a dihalide 'X', with an ester 'Y', followed by acidic hydrolysis. Identify the correct pair of starting materials 'X' and 'Y'.
questions.solution:
The target molecule is 1-phenylcyclopentan-1-ol, which contains a five-membered ring with a phenyl group and a hydroxyl group on the same carbon atom.

In the reaction of a di-Grignard reagent with an ester, the ester carbonyl carbon becomes the tertiary carbon bearing the hydroxyl group in the final product. The ester must also provide the substituent attached to this carbon. Since the product has a phenyl group on the hydroxyl-bearing carbon, the ester must be a benzoate ester (e.g., ethyl benzoate, $\text{PhCOOEt}$).

The remaining four carbon atoms of the five-membered ring must originate from the di-Grignard reagent. Therefore, the di-Grignard reagent must be formed from a four-carbon dihalide, which is 1,4-dibromobutane.

Reaction sequence:
1. 1,4-dibromobutane reacts with Mg to form $\text{BrMg-(CH}_2\text{)}_4\text{-MgBr}$.
2. One nucleophilic end attacks ethyl benzoate, expelling the ethoxide leaving group to form the ketone intermediate $\text{Ph-CO-(CH}_2\text{)}_4\text{-MgBr}$.
3. The other nucleophilic end attacks the newly formed carbonyl intramolecularly, closing a five-membered ring.
4. Acidic hydrolysis yields 1-phenylcyclopentan-1-ol.

Answer: 'X' = 1,4-dibromobutane ; 'Y' = ethyl benzoate

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alkyl halides yields 2-methylpentan-2-ol as the major product upon hydrolysis with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$?
questions.question: Which of the following alkyl halides yields 2-methylpentan-2-ol as the major product upon hydrolysis with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$?
questions.solution:
Retrosynthetic analysis of 2-methylpentan-2-ol shows that the $\text{OH}$ group is at the tertiary C2 position. This indicates that the reaction proceeds via a tertiary carbocation at C2.

Let us analyze the given options:
For 3-chloro-2-methylpentane, ionization of the $\text{C-Cl}$ bond yields a secondary carbocation at C3. A 1,2-hydride shift from the adjacent tertiary C2 carbon generates a more stable tertiary carbocation at C2. Nucleophilic attack by $\text{H}_2\text{O}/\text{OH}^-$ on this tertiary carbocation yields 2-methylpentan-2-ol as the major product.

For 2-chloro-3-methylpentane, the secondary carbocation at C2 undergoes a 1,2-hydride shift from C3 to form a tertiary carbocation at C3, yielding 3-methylpentan-3-ol.

For 2-chloro-4-methylpentane, no adjacent tertiary carbon is present, so it primarily yields the unrearranged secondary alcohol.

For 3-chloro-3-methylpentane, the tertiary carbocation at C3 directly yields 3-methylpentan-3-ol.

Answer: 3-chloro-2-methylpentane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When 1-(1-phenylcyclobutyl)ethan-1-ol is heated with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, the major organic product formed is:
questions.question: When 1-(1-phenylcyclobutyl)ethan-1-ol is heated with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, the major organic product formed is:
questions.solution:
Protonation of the hydroxyl group of 1-(1-phenylcyclobutyl)ethan-1-ol followed by the loss of a water molecule generates a secondary carbocation at the side chain.

The highly strained four-membered cyclobutane ring undergoes expansion to relieve ring strain. A C-C bond migrates to the secondary carbocation, expanding the ring to a five-membered cyclopentane ring. This shifts the positive charge to the carbon bearing the phenyl group, forming a highly stable tertiary benzylic carbocation (1-phenyl-2-methylcyclopentyl cation).

Finally, the elimination of a proton ($\text{H}^+$) occurs. According to Saytzeff's rule, the most substituted alkene is formed as the major product. The proton is lost from the adjacent carbon bearing the methyl group, yielding the tetrasubstituted alkene, 1-methyl-2-phenylcyclopent-1-ene.

Answer: 1-methyl-2-phenylcyclopent-1-ene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
$p$-Cresol (4-methylphenol) is subjected to two separate reactions:
Reaction 1: $p$-cresol reacts with $\text{CHCl}_3$ and aqueous $\text{NaOH}$, followed by acidification to yield major product A.
Reaction 2: $p$-cresol reacts with $\text{Br}_2$ in $\text{CS}_2$ at $273 \text{ K}$ to yield major product B.

Identify the major products A and B.
questions.question:
$p$-Cresol (4-methylphenol) is subjected to two separate reactions:
Reaction 1: $p$-cresol reacts with $\text{CHCl}_3$ and aqueous $\text{NaOH}$, followed by acidification to yield major product A.
Reaction 2: $p$-cresol reacts with $\text{Br}_2$ in $\text{CS}_2$ at $273 \text{ K}$ to yield major product B.

Identify the major products A and B.
questions.solution:
In $p$-cresol, the $-\text{OH}$ group is strongly activating and ortho/para directing, whereas the $-\text{CH}_3$ group is weakly activating and ortho/para directing. The directing effect of the $-\text{OH}$ group dominates.

Since the para position is blocked by the $-\text{CH}_3$ group, electrophilic substitution must occur at the position ortho to the $-\text{OH}$ group.

Reaction 1 is the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, which introduces a formyl group ($-\text{CHO}$) ortho to the $-\text{OH}$ group. Thus, product A is 2-hydroxy-5-methylbenzaldehyde.

Reaction 2 is bromination in a non-polar solvent ($\text{CS}_2$) at low temperature, which leads to monobromination ortho to the $-\text{OH}$ group. Thus, product B is 2-bromo-4-methylphenol.

Answer: A is 2-hydroxy-5-methylbenzaldehyde; B is 2-bromo-4-methylphenol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An unknown secondary alcohol A is heated with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to yield a major alkene B. When alkene B is treated with a cold, dilute aqueous solution of $\text{KMnO}_4$ (Baeyer's reagent), it yields butane-2,3-diol. The starting alcohol A is:
questions.question: An unknown secondary alcohol A is heated with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to yield a major alkene B. When alkene B is treated with a cold, dilute aqueous solution of $\text{KMnO}_4$ (Baeyer's reagent), it yields butane-2,3-diol. The starting alcohol A is:
questions.solution:
The final product is butane-2,3-diol, which is a vicinal diol.

Vicinal diols are formed by the syn-hydroxylation of alkenes using Baeyer's reagent (cold, dilute aqueous $\text{KMnO}_4$).

Working backwards, the alkene B that yields butane-2,3-diol upon hydroxylation must be but-2-ene.

Alkene B (but-2-ene) is formed as the major product of the acid-catalyzed dehydration of alcohol A.

According to Saytzeff's rule, the dehydration of butan-2-ol yields but-2-ene as the major, more substituted alkene.

Therefore, the secondary alcohol A is butan-2-ol.

Answer: Butan-2-ol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following reaction sequence starting with 2,2,6-trimethylcyclohexan-1-ol:

$\text{2,2,6-trimethylcyclohexan-1-ol} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{conc. H}_2\text{SO}_4} \text{B (Major Product)}$

$\text{B} \xrightarrow[\text{Zn/H}_2\text{O}]{\text{O}_3} \text{C}$

$\text{C} \xrightarrow[\text{then H}_3\text{O}^+]{\text{excess I}_2 / \text{NaOH}} \text{D}$

What is the IUPAC name of the final product D?
questions.question:
Consider the following reaction sequence starting with 2,2,6-trimethylcyclohexan-1-ol:

$\text{2,2,6-trimethylcyclohexan-1-ol} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{conc. H}_2\text{SO}_4} \text{B (Major Product)}$

$\text{B} \xrightarrow[\text{Zn/H}_2\text{O}]{\text{O}_3} \text{C}$

$\text{C} \xrightarrow[\text{then H}_3\text{O}^+]{\text{excess I}_2 / \text{NaOH}} \text{D}$

What is the IUPAC name of the final product D?
questions.solution:
Dehydration of 2,2,6-trimethylcyclohexan-1-ol with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ generates a secondary carbocation at C-1.

To relieve the steric strain of the gem-dimethyl group and form a more stable product, a 1,2-methyl shift occurs from C-2 to C-1, rather than a hydride shift from C-6.

Elimination of a proton yields the most stable tetrasubstituted alkene, 1,2,3-trimethylcyclohexene (Product B).

Reductive ozonolysis ($\text{O}_3$, $\text{Zn/H}_2\text{O}$) of 1,2,3-trimethylcyclohexene cleaves the double bond to form a diketone. The ring opens to give 3-methyloctane-2,7-dione (Product C).

Product C contains two terminal methyl ketone groups ($\text{-COCH}_3$). Treatment with excess $\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$ initiates the iodoform reaction at both ends, cleaving the terminal methyl groups as $\text{CHI}_3$.

Subsequent acidification ($\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$) converts the resulting carboxylate salts into carboxylic acid groups, yielding 2-methylhexanedioic acid (Product D).

Answer: 2-methylhexanedioic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Acetophenone is subjected to the following sequence of reactions:
(i) $CH_3MgBr$, followed by $H_3O^+$
(ii) Conc. $H_2SO_4$, $\Delta$
(iii) $B_2H_6$ followed by $H_2O_2 / OH^-$
(iv) Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC)

The major product formed at the end of the sequence is :
questions.question:
Acetophenone is subjected to the following sequence of reactions:
(i) $CH_3MgBr$, followed by $H_3O^+$
(ii) Conc. $H_2SO_4$, $\Delta$
(iii) $B_2H_6$ followed by $H_2O_2 / OH^-$
(iv) Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC)

The major product formed at the end of the sequence is :
questions.solution:
Acetophenone reacts with methylmagnesium bromide (Grignard reagent) followed by acidic workup to undergo nucleophilic addition, forming a tertiary alcohol, 2-phenyl-2-propanol.

Heating 2-phenyl-2-propanol with concentrated $H_2SO_4$ causes acid-catalyzed dehydration, yielding 2-phenylpropene as the major product.

Hydroboration-oxidation of 2-phenylpropene with $B_2H_6$ followed by $H_2O_2 / OH^-$ results in anti-Markovnikov addition of water, producing the primary alcohol, 2-phenyl-1-propanol.

Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) is a mild oxidizing agent that selectively oxidizes primary alcohols to aldehydes without further oxidation to carboxylic acids. Thus, 2-phenyl-1-propanol is oxidized to 2-phenylpropanal.

Answer: 2-Phenylpropanal

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following compounds:
(P) 1-(4-methoxyphenyl)ethan-1-ol
(Q) 1-phenylethan-1-ol
(R) 1-(4-nitrophenyl)ethan-1-ol
(S) Phenol

The decreasing order of their rate of acid-catalyzed dehydration is:
questions.question:
Consider the following compounds:
(P) 1-(4-methoxyphenyl)ethan-1-ol
(Q) 1-phenylethan-1-ol
(R) 1-(4-nitrophenyl)ethan-1-ol
(S) Phenol

The decreasing order of their rate of acid-catalyzed dehydration is:
questions.solution:
The rate of acid-catalyzed dehydration of alcohols depends on the stability of the intermediate carbocation formed after the protonation and loss of a water molecule.

For (P), the intermediate is the 1-(4-methoxyphenyl)ethyl cation, which is highly stabilized by the +M effect of the methoxy group.

For (Q), the intermediate is the 1-phenylethyl cation, stabilized by resonance with the benzene ring.

For (R), the intermediate is the 1-(4-nitrophenyl)ethyl cation, which is strongly destabilized by the -M and -I effects of the nitro group.

For (S), phenol does not undergo acid-catalyzed dehydration because the cleavage of the C-O bond would produce a highly unstable phenyl cation.

Therefore, the stability order of the carbocations is $P > Q > R$, and S does not react.

The decreasing order of the rate of dehydration is $P > Q > R > S$.

Answer: $P > Q > R > S$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following reaction sequence:
2-methylhexane-1,5-diol $\xrightarrow{\text{PCC (excess)}}$ P $\xrightarrow[\text{H}^{+}]{\text{Ethylene glycol (1 eq.)}}$ Q $\xrightarrow[\text{2. H}_3\text{O}^{+}]{\text{1. CH}_3\text{MgBr (excess)}}$ R $\xrightarrow{\text{NaBH}_4, \text{ EtOH}}$ S

The number of chiral carbon atoms in compound S is _______.
questions.question:
Consider the following reaction sequence:
2-methylhexane-1,5-diol $\xrightarrow{\text{PCC (excess)}}$ P $\xrightarrow[\text{H}^{+}]{\text{Ethylene glycol (1 eq.)}}$ Q $\xrightarrow[\text{2. H}_3\text{O}^{+}]{\text{1. CH}_3\text{MgBr (excess)}}$ R $\xrightarrow{\text{NaBH}_4, \text{ EtOH}}$ S

The number of chiral carbon atoms in compound S is _______.
questions.solution:
PCC is an oxidizing agent that converts primary alcohols to aldehydes and secondary alcohols to ketones. Thus, 2-methylhexane-1,5-diol is oxidized to 2-methyl-5-oxohexanal (P).

Aldehydes are more reactive towards nucleophilic addition than ketones. Treatment of P with 1 equivalent of ethylene glycol in acidic medium selectively protects the aldehyde group, forming an acetal (Q).

The Grignard reagent ($\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$) attacks the unprotected ketone group, converting it into a tertiary alcohol. The subsequent acidic workup ($\text{H}_3\text{O}^{+}$) hydrolyzes the acetal back to the aldehyde. Thus, R is 5-hydroxy-2,5-dimethylhexanal.

$\text{NaBH}_4$ reduces the aldehyde group to a primary alcohol but does not affect the tertiary alcohol. The final product S is 2,5-dimethylhexane-1,5-diol, with the structure $\text{HO-CH}_2\text{-CH(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-C(OH)(CH}_3)_2$.

In compound S, only the C2 carbon atom is bonded to four different groups ($\text{-H}$, $\text{-CH}_3$, $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$, and $\text{-CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{C(OH)(CH}_3)_2$). Therefore, there is exactly $1$ chiral carbon atom.

Answer: $1$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When 2-methylhept-5-en-2-ol is treated with catalytic $\text{H}^+$ and heat, followed by the addition of $\text{HBr}$, a major cyclic product is formed. The IUPAC name of this major product is:
questions.question: When 2-methylhept-5-en-2-ol is treated with catalytic $\text{H}^+$ and heat, followed by the addition of $\text{HBr}$, a major cyclic product is formed. The IUPAC name of this major product is:
questions.solution:
Acid-catalyzed dehydration of 2-methylhept-5-en-2-ol generates a stable tertiary carbocation at C2.

Intramolecular cyclization occurs as the C5=C6 pi bond attacks the C2 carbocation. Attack by C6 forms a kinetically and thermodynamically favored 5-membered ring, leaving a secondary carbocation at C5. Attack by C5 is disfavored as it would form a more strained 4-membered ring.

The secondary carbocation at C5 is adjacent to C6, which bears a methyl group and a hydrogen atom. A 1,2-hydride shift occurs from C6 to C5, rearranging the secondary carbocation into a more stable tertiary carbocation at C6.

The bromide ion ($\text{Br}^-$) then attacks the tertiary carbocation at C6, yielding 1-bromo-1,2,2-trimethylcyclopentane as the major product.

Answer: 1-bromo-1,2,2-trimethylcyclopentane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When phenol is treated with carbon tetrachloride ($\text{CCl}_4$) and aqueous $\text{NaOH}$, an intermediate $Y$ is formed. Subsequent alkaline hydrolysis and acidification of $Y$ yields salicylic acid as the major product. The chemical name of the intermediate $Y$ is :
questions.question: When phenol is treated with carbon tetrachloride ($\text{CCl}_4$) and aqueous $\text{NaOH}$, an intermediate $Y$ is formed. Subsequent alkaline hydrolysis and acidification of $Y$ yields salicylic acid as the major product. The chemical name of the intermediate $Y$ is :
questions.solution:
In the Reimer-Tiemann carboxylation reaction, phenol reacts with $\text{CCl}_4$ in the presence of a strong base like $\text{NaOH}$.

The base deprotonates phenol to form the phenoxide ion. The electrophile generated from $\text{CCl}_4$ attacks the ortho position of the phenoxide ring.

Since $\text{CCl}_4$ has four chlorine atoms, the intermediate formed before hydrolysis contains a $-\text{CCl}_3$ group. Furthermore, because the reaction medium is strongly alkaline, the phenolic oxygen remains deprotonated as a sodium salt.

Thus, the intermediate $Y$ is sodium 2-(trichloromethyl)phenoxide.

Answer: Sodium 2-(trichloromethyl)phenoxide

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the major product $\mathrm{Z}$ in the following reaction sequence:

Chlorobenzene $\xrightarrow[\text{300 atm}]{\text{NaOH, 623 K}} \mathrm{X} \xrightarrow[\text{then } \mathrm{H}^{+}]{\text{CO}_{2}\text{, 400 K}} \mathrm{Y} \xrightarrow{\text{Acetic anhydride, } \mathrm{H}^{+}} \mathrm{Z}$
questions.question:
Identify the major product $\mathrm{Z}$ in the following reaction sequence:

Chlorobenzene $\xrightarrow[\text{300 atm}]{\text{NaOH, 623 K}} \mathrm{X} \xrightarrow[\text{then } \mathrm{H}^{+}]{\text{CO}_{2}\text{, 400 K}} \mathrm{Y} \xrightarrow{\text{Acetic anhydride, } \mathrm{H}^{+}} \mathrm{Z}$
questions.solution:
Chlorobenzene reacts with aqueous $\mathrm{NaOH}$ at $623\text{ K}$ and $300\text{ atm}$ to form sodium phenoxide via the Dow process. Thus, $\mathrm{X}$ is sodium phenoxide.

Sodium phenoxide undergoes Kolbe's reaction with $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ at $400\text{ K}$ followed by acidification to yield 2-hydroxybenzoic acid (salicylic acid). Thus, $\mathrm{Y}$ is salicylic acid.

Salicylic acid reacts with acetic anhydride in the presence of an acid catalyst to undergo acetylation at the phenolic $-\mathrm{OH}$ group, forming 2-acetoxybenzoic acid (acetylsalicylic acid, commonly known as aspirin). Thus, $\mathrm{Z}$ is 2-acetoxybenzoic acid.

Answer: 2-Acetoxybenzoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 2,3-Dihydrobenzofuran is heated with excess concentrated HI. The major product formed in this reaction is:
questions.question: 2,3-Dihydrobenzofuran is heated with excess concentrated HI. The major product formed in this reaction is:
questions.solution:
2,3-Dihydrobenzofuran is a bicyclic compound containing a cyclic ether fused to a benzene ring. The ether oxygen is bonded to an $sp^2$ hybridized aromatic carbon (aryl-oxygen bond) and an $sp^3$ hybridized aliphatic carbon (alkyl-oxygen bond).

When treated with concentrated HI and heated, ether cleavage occurs. The aryl-oxygen bond has partial double bond character due to the delocalization of the oxygen's lone pair into the aromatic ring, making it strong and resistant to cleavage.

Therefore, the cleavage exclusively takes place at the alkyl-oxygen bond. The ring opens, with the oxygen remaining attached to the benzene ring to form a phenol, and the iodide ion attacking the aliphatic carbon to form an alkyl iodide.

The resulting structure has a hydroxyl group and a 2-iodoethyl group on adjacent carbons of the benzene ring. Thus, the major product is 2-(2-iodoethyl)phenol.

Answer: 2-(2-Iodoethyl)phenol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An organic compound 'A' with the molecular formula $\text{C}_7\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$ reacts with hydroxylamine to form compound 'B'. Upon heating with $\text{P}_2\text{O}_5$, compound 'B' yields 2-hydroxybenzonitrile. Which of the following sets of reagents will produce compound 'A' as the major product when reacted with phenol?
questions.question: An organic compound 'A' with the molecular formula $\text{C}_7\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$ reacts with hydroxylamine to form compound 'B'. Upon heating with $\text{P}_2\text{O}_5$, compound 'B' yields 2-hydroxybenzonitrile. Which of the following sets of reagents will produce compound 'A' as the major product when reacted with phenol?
options: $\text{CO}_2$ and aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ under pressure, followed by acidification
questions.solution:
Working backwards from the final product, heating an oxime with a dehydrating agent like $\text{P}_2\text{O}_5$ yields a nitrile. Since the product is 2-hydroxybenzonitrile, compound 'B' must be 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde oxime.

Compound 'B' is formed by the reaction of 'A' with hydroxylamine ($\text{NH}_2\text{OH}$). Thus, compound 'A' is 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde (also known as salicylaldehyde). The molecular formula of salicylaldehyde is $\text{C}_7\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$, which matches the given data.

To synthesize salicylaldehyde as the major product starting from phenol, the Reimer-Tiemann reaction is employed. The reagents required for this transformation are chloroform ($\text{CHCl}_3$) and aqueous sodium hydroxide ($\text{NaOH}$), followed by acidification.

(Note: $\text{CO}_2$ and aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ are used in Kolbe's reaction to yield salicylic acid, while $\text{HCN}/\text{HCl}/\text{AlCl}_3$ is used in the Gattermann reaction which typically yields 4-hydroxybenzaldehyde as the major product).

Answer: $\text{CHCl}_3$ and aqueous $\text{NaOH}$, followed by acidification

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following compounds:
Phenol, 4-Nitrophenol, 2,4-Dinitrophenol, 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol, Benzoic acid, Benzenesulphonic acid, 2-Methylphenol, 2-Hydroxybenzoic acid.

The number of compounds that will dissolve in both aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ and aqueous $\text{NaHCO}_3$ solutions is _____.
questions.question:
Consider the following compounds:
Phenol, 4-Nitrophenol, 2,4-Dinitrophenol, 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol, Benzoic acid, Benzenesulphonic acid, 2-Methylphenol, 2-Hydroxybenzoic acid.

The number of compounds that will dissolve in both aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ and aqueous $\text{NaHCO}_3$ solutions is _____.
questions.solution:
For a compound to dissolve in both aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ and aqueous $\text{NaHCO}_3$, it must be a stronger acid than carbonic acid ($\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3$).

Carboxylic acids and sulphonic acids are stronger acids than carbonic acid. Therefore, Benzoic acid, Benzenesulphonic acid, and 2-Hydroxybenzoic acid (which contains a carboxylic acid group) will dissolve in both.

Simple phenols are weaker acids than carbonic acid and do not dissolve in $\text{NaHCO}_3$. Thus, Phenol and 2-Methylphenol dissolve in $\text{NaOH}$ but not in $\text{NaHCO}_3$.

The presence of electron-withdrawing groups increases the acidity of phenols. 4-Nitrophenol is still not acidic enough to dissolve in $\text{NaHCO}_3$. However, with two or three nitro groups, the acidity increases significantly. 2,4-Dinitrophenol and 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol (picric acid) are stronger acids than carbonic acid and will dissolve in both solutions.

Total compounds dissolving in both = 2,4-Dinitrophenol, 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol, Benzoic acid, Benzenesulphonic acid, and 2-Hydroxybenzoic acid.

The number of such compounds is 5.

Answer: $5$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When 1-(2-methoxypropan-2-yl)-1-methylcyclobutane is treated with excess heated $\text{HI}$, the major organic product formed is:
questions.question: When 1-(2-methoxypropan-2-yl)-1-methylcyclobutane is treated with excess heated $\text{HI}$, the major organic product formed is:
questions.solution:
In the presence of excess heated $\text{HI}$, the ether undergoes cleavage via an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ mechanism because it contains a tertiary alkyl group. The oxygen is protonated, and the C-O bond breaks to form a stable tertiary carbocation, the 2-(1-methylcyclobutyl)propan-2-yl cation, along with methanol (which further reacts with $\text{HI}$ to form methyl iodide).

The formed carbocation is adjacent to a highly strained four-membered cyclobutane ring. To relieve ring strain, a C-C bond of the cyclobutane ring migrates to the positively charged carbon, expanding the ring to a five-membered cyclopentane ring.

This ring expansion shifts the positive charge to the adjacent carbon, forming the 1,2,2-trimethylcyclopentyl cation, which is also a stable tertiary carbocation.

Finally, the iodide ion ($\text{I}^-$) acts as a nucleophile and attacks this rearranged tertiary carbocation to yield the major substitution product, 1-iodo-1,2,2-trimethylcyclopentane.

Answer: 1-iodo-1,2,2-trimethylcyclopentane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When 5-bromo-1,2-epoxypentane is treated with magnesium turnings in dry ether followed by acidic hydrolysis, the major organic product formed is:
questions.question: When 5-bromo-1,2-epoxypentane is treated with magnesium turnings in dry ether followed by acidic hydrolysis, the major organic product formed is:
questions.solution:
The reaction proceeds via the formation of a Grignard reagent followed by an intramolecular nucleophilic attack.

1. Magnesium inserts into the primary $\text{C-Br}$ bond of 5-bromo-1,2-epoxypentane to form the Grignard reagent, 5-(bromomagnesio)-1,2-epoxypentane.
2. The nucleophilic carbon (C5) can attack the epoxide intramolecularly. There are two possible sites for attack:
- Attack at the less substituted carbon (C1) of the epoxide opens the ring to form a 5-membered cyclic alkoxide.
- Attack at the more substituted carbon (C2) would form a strained 4-membered ring with a primary alkoxide (cyclobutylmethoxide).
3. Nucleophilic opening of epoxides under basic/neutral conditions (like Grignard reactions) preferentially occurs at the less sterically hindered carbon (C1) via an $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ mechanism. Furthermore, the formation of a 5-membered ring is thermodynamically and kinetically favored over a 4-membered ring due to lower ring strain.
4. Attack at C1 yields the cyclopentanoxide intermediate, which upon acidic hydrolysis gives cyclopentanol.

Answer: Cyclopentanol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Compound A is 5-oxohexanal. One mole of A is reacted with one mole of $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$ in ether followed by hydrolysis with water to give major product B. Compound B is then treated with an excess of $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{NaOH}$, followed by acidification, to yield compound C.

The number of moles of $\text{NaOH}$ required to completely neutralize $1$ mole of compound C is _______.
questions.question:
Compound A is 5-oxohexanal. One mole of A is reacted with one mole of $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$ in ether followed by hydrolysis with water to give major product B. Compound B is then treated with an excess of $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{NaOH}$, followed by acidification, to yield compound C.

The number of moles of $\text{NaOH}$ required to completely neutralize $1$ mole of compound C is _______.
questions.solution:
Compound A is 5-oxohexanal, which contains both an aldehyde and a ketone group. Aldehydes are more electrophilic and sterically less hindered than ketones. Thus, 1 equivalent of $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$ selectively attacks the aldehyde group. After hydrolysis, the major product B is 6-hydroxyheptan-2-one.

Compound B is treated with excess $\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$ (haloform reagent). The reagent first acts as an oxidizing agent, oxidizing the secondary alcohol at C6 to a ketone, forming heptane-2,6-dione.

Heptane-2,6-dione has two methyl ketone groups. The excess $\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$ performs the haloform reaction on both ends, cleaving them to yield the dicarboxylate salt, which upon acidification gives pentanedioic acid (glutaric acid), $\text{HOOC-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-COOH}$, as compound C.

Compound C is a dicarboxylic acid. Therefore, 1 mole of C requires 2 moles of $\text{NaOH}$ for complete neutralization.

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
An alcohol, 3,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol, is subjected to the following reaction sequence:
(i) Conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, $\Delta$
(ii) $\text{O}_3$, $\text{Zn/H}_2\text{O}$

The major final product(s) of this sequence is/are:
questions.question:
An alcohol, 3,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol, is subjected to the following reaction sequence:
(i) Conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, $\Delta$
(ii) $\text{O}_3$, $\text{Zn/H}_2\text{O}$

The major final product(s) of this sequence is/are:
questions.solution:
In the first step, 3,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol undergoes acid-catalyzed dehydration. Protonation and loss of water form a secondary carbocation: $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2-\text{CH}^+-\text{CH}_3$.

This secondary carbocation undergoes a 1,2-methyl shift from the adjacent quaternary carbon to form a more stable tertiary carbocation: $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}^+(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_3$.

According to Zaitsev's rule, elimination of a proton occurs from the adjacent carbon that yields the most substituted alkene. Deprotonation from C3 gives 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene, $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_3$, as the major product.

In the second step, 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene undergoes reductive ozonolysis ($\text{O}_3$ followed by $\text{Zn/H}_2\text{O}$). The tetrasubstituted carbon-carbon double bond is cleaved to form two molecules of ketones.

The cleavage of 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene yields two molecules of propan-2-one (acetone), $\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_3$.

Answer: Propan-2-one

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A molecule (X), $2$-(allyloxy)propene, under mild acidic conditions is hydrolysed to produce (Y) and (Z). Identify the correct statements about (Y) and (Z).

A. (Y) and (Z) are structural isomers.
B. Both (Y) and (Z) decolorize bromine water.
C. Only one of them forms a yellow precipitate with NaOI.
D. Only one of them gives effervescence with Na metal.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.question:
A molecule (X), $2$-(allyloxy)propene, under mild acidic conditions is hydrolysed to produce (Y) and (Z). Identify the correct statements about (Y) and (Z).

A. (Y) and (Z) are structural isomers.
B. Both (Y) and (Z) decolorize bromine water.
C. Only one of them forms a yellow precipitate with NaOI.
D. Only one of them gives effervescence with Na metal.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The structure of $2$-(allyloxy)propene is $CH_2=C(CH_3)-O-CH_2-CH=CH_2$.

Under mild acidic conditions, the enol ether linkage is hydrolysed. The cleavage occurs at the $O-C(sp^2)$ bond. The enol ether part is converted to a ketone, and the alkoxy part becomes an alcohol.
The hydrolysis yields acetone, $CH_3COCH_3$, and allyl alcohol, $HO-CH_2-CH=CH_2$.

Statement A: Acetone and allyl alcohol both have the same molecular formula $C_3H_6O$. They are structural isomers. Statement A is true.

Statement B: Allyl alcohol contains a carbon-carbon double bond and decolorizes bromine water. Acetone does not react with bromine water. Statement B is false.

Statement C: Acetone is a methyl ketone and gives a positive iodoform test (forming a yellow precipitate with NaOI). Allyl alcohol does not give this test. Statement C is true.

Statement D: Allyl alcohol reacts with active metals like Na to release $H_2$ gas (effervescence). Acetone does not react with Na metal. Statement D is true.

Therefore, the correct statements are A, C, and D.

Answer: A, C and D Only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Phenol reacts with $\text{Br}_2$ in $\text{CS}_2$ at $273 \text{ K}$ to give a major product P.
P reacts with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ followed by $\text{CH}_3\text{I}$ to give Q.
Q is heated with concentrated $\text{HI}$ to give an aromatic product R and an aliphatic product S.

Identify the structures of P, Q, and R.
questions.question:
Phenol reacts with $\text{Br}_2$ in $\text{CS}_2$ at $273 \text{ K}$ to give a major product P.
P reacts with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ followed by $\text{CH}_3\text{I}$ to give Q.
Q is heated with concentrated $\text{HI}$ to give an aromatic product R and an aliphatic product S.

Identify the structures of P, Q, and R.
options: P is 2,4,6-tribromophenol; Q is 2,4,6-tribromoanisole; R is 2,4,6-tribromophenol
P is 4-bromophenol; Q is 4-bromoanisole; R is 4-bromophenol
P is 4-bromophenol; Q is 4-bromoanisole; R is 1-bromo-4-iodobenzene
P is 4-bromophenol; Q is 4-bromoanisole; R is 4-iodophenol
questions.solution:
Phenol reacts with $\text{Br}_2$ in a non-polar solvent ($\text{CS}_2$) at low temperature to undergo monohalogenation. The major product P is 4-bromophenol.

4-bromophenol reacts with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ to form sodium 4-bromophenoxide, which then undergoes Williamson ether synthesis with $\text{CH}_3\text{I}$ to form 4-bromoanisole (Q).

When 4-bromoanisole is heated with concentrated $\text{HI}$, the ether linkage is cleaved. Since the aryl-oxygen bond has partial double bond character due to resonance and is stronger, the cleavage occurs at the alkyl-oxygen bond. This yields 4-bromophenol (R) and methyl iodide (S).

Answer: P is 4-bromophenol; Q is 4-bromoanisole; R is 4-bromophenol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are four compounds :
A. n-Butane
B. Methoxyethane
C. Propan-1-ol
D. Butan-1-ol

The correct increasing order of their boiling points is :
questions.question:
Given below are four compounds :
A. n-Butane
B. Methoxyethane
C. Propan-1-ol
D. Butan-1-ol

The correct increasing order of their boiling points is :
questions.solution:
The boiling point of organic compounds depends on the magnitude of intermolecular forces.

n-Butane (A) is a non-polar hydrocarbon and has only weak van der Waals dispersion forces, giving it the lowest boiling point.

Methoxyethane (B) is an ether. It is slightly polar and experiences weak dipole-dipole interactions, making its boiling point higher than that of n-butane.

Propan-1-ol (C) and Butan-1-ol (D) are alcohols and can form strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds, resulting in significantly higher boiling points than ethers and alkanes of comparable molecular mass.

Between Propan-1-ol and Butan-1-ol, Butan-1-ol has a larger carbon chain (higher molecular mass and greater surface area), which leads to stronger van der Waals forces. Thus, Butan-1-ol has a higher boiling point than Propan-1-ol.

Therefore, the correct increasing order of boiling points is A < B < C < D.

Answer: A < B < C < D

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: During the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, when phenol is treated with chloroform in the presence of aqueous sodium hydroxide, an electrophile is generated in situ which attacks the aromatic ring. The identity of this electrophile is:
questions.question: During the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, when phenol is treated with chloroform in the presence of aqueous sodium hydroxide, an electrophile is generated in situ which attacks the aromatic ring. The identity of this electrophile is:
questions.solution:
In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, the base ($OH^-$) abstracts a proton from chloroform ($CHCl_3$) to form the trichloromethyl carbanion ($CCl_3^-$).

$CHCl_3 + OH^- \rightleftharpoons CCl_3^- + H_2O$

This carbanion readily undergoes alpha-elimination by losing a chloride ion to generate dichlorocarbene ($:CCl_2$), which is a neutral, electron-deficient species.

$CCl_3^- \rightarrow :CCl_2 + Cl^-$

The dichlorocarbene acts as the electrophile and attacks the electron-rich phenoxide ring to eventually yield 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde after hydrolysis.

Answer: $:CCl_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following reaction sequence:

4-Methoxybenzaldehyde $\xrightarrow{\text{HNO}_3 / \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4}$ A $\xrightarrow{\text{NH}_2\text{OH}}$ B $\xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{SOCl}_2}$ C

The major product 'C' is:
questions.question:
Consider the following reaction sequence:

4-Methoxybenzaldehyde $\xrightarrow{\text{HNO}_3 / \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4}$ A $\xrightarrow{\text{NH}_2\text{OH}}$ B $\xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{SOCl}_2}$ C

The major product 'C' is:
questions.solution:
In the first step, nitration of 4-methoxybenzaldehyde takes place. The methoxy group ($\text{-OCH}_3$) is activating and ortho/para directing, while the aldehyde group ($\text{-CHO}$) is deactivating and meta directing. Both groups synergistically direct the incoming electrophile ($\text{NO}_2^+$) to the position ortho to the methoxy group (which is meta to the aldehyde group). Thus, product A is 4-methoxy-3-nitrobenzaldehyde.

In the second step, the aldehyde reacts with hydroxylamine ($\text{NH}_2\text{OH}$) to form an oxime (product B).

In the final step, heating the oxime with thionyl chloride ($\text{SOCl}_2$) causes dehydration, converting the oxime group into a nitrile group. The ether linkage remains unaffected. Therefore, the final major product C is 4-methoxy-3-nitrobenzonitrile.

Answer: 4-Methoxy-3-nitrobenzonitrile

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An acyclic alcohol, 2,2,4-trimethylpentan-3-ol, is heated with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$. What is the IUPAC name of the major alkene product formed?
questions.question: An acyclic alcohol, 2,2,4-trimethylpentan-3-ol, is heated with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$. What is the IUPAC name of the major alkene product formed?
questions.solution:
Protonation of 2,2,4-trimethylpentan-3-ol and subsequent loss of a water molecule generates a secondary carbocation at C-3: $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2-\text{CH}^+-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$.

This carbocation can undergo either a 1,2-hydride shift from C-4 or a 1,2-methyl shift from C-2.

A 1,2-hydride shift would yield a tertiary carbocation that eliminates to form 2,4,4-trimethylpent-2-ene, a trisubstituted alkene.

However, a 1,2-methyl shift from the highly sterically hindered tert-butyl group yields a different tertiary carbocation: $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}^+(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$.

Elimination of a proton from this rearranged carbocation yields 2,3,4-trimethylpent-2-ene, which is a tetrasubstituted alkene.

The methyl shift is favored because it relieves severe steric strain and produces a more thermodynamically stable (Saytzeff) alkene. Thus, 2,3,4-trimethylpent-2-ene is the major product.

Answer: 2,3,4-trimethylpent-2-ene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When 4-(methoxymethyl)anisole is heated with excess concentrated HI, the major aromatic product formed is:
questions.question: When 4-(methoxymethyl)anisole is heated with excess concentrated HI, the major aromatic product formed is:
questions.solution:
The given molecule, 4-(methoxymethyl)anisole, contains two different ether linkages: an aryl alkyl ether ($-O-CH_3$ attached directly to the benzene ring) and a benzyl alkyl ether ($-CH_2-O-CH_3$).

When heated with excess concentrated HI:
1. For the aryl alkyl ether, the $Ar-O$ bond has partial double bond character due to resonance and is stronger than the $O-CH_3$ bond. Thus, cleavage occurs at the $O-CH_3$ bond, yielding a phenol ($-OH$) and methyl iodide ($CH_3I$).
2. For the benzyl alkyl ether, the $Ar-CH_2-O$ bond cleaves readily to form a stable benzyl carbocation intermediate, which is attacked by $I^-$ to give a benzyl iodide ($-CH_2-I$) and methanol ($CH_3OH$).
3. Since excess HI is used, the methanol formed also reacts to give methyl iodide ($CH_3I$).

Combining these reactions, the methoxy group on the ring becomes a hydroxyl group, and the methoxymethyl group becomes an iodomethyl group. Therefore, the major aromatic product is 4-(iodomethyl)phenol.

Answer: 4-(Iodomethyl)phenol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Phenol is subjected to the following sequence of reactions:

(i) $CHCl_3$, aq. $NaOH$, followed by $H_3O^+\rightarrow$ Major Product A
(ii) $NaBH_4$ in ethanol → Major Product B

The IUPAC name of the final major product B is:
questions.question:
Phenol is subjected to the following sequence of reactions:

(i) $CHCl_3$, aq. $NaOH$, followed by $H_3O^+\rightarrow$ Major Product A
(ii) $NaBH_4$ in ethanol → Major Product B

The IUPAC name of the final major product B is:
questions.solution:
Step (i) is the Reimer-Tiemann reaction. Phenol reacts with chloroform and aqueous sodium hydroxide, followed by acidification, to form 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde (salicylaldehyde) as the major product A. The ortho-isomer is the major product due to stabilization by intramolecular hydrogen bonding.

Step (ii) involves the reduction of product A with sodium borohydride ($NaBH_4$). $NaBH_4$ is a mild, chemoselective reducing agent that reduces aldehydes and ketones to their corresponding alcohols, but it does not reduce the aromatic ring, carboxylic acids, or the phenolic $-OH$ group.

Therefore, the formyl group ($-CHO$) in 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde is reduced to a primary alcohol ($-CH_2OH$). The resulting product B is 2-(hydroxymethyl)phenol.

Answer: 2-(Hydroxymethyl)phenol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the substrate 3,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol. It is subjected to two separate reactions:
Reaction 1: Treatment with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and heat to give major product A.
Reaction 2: Treatment with $\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}$ and pyridine to give major product B.
Identify the IUPAC names of the major products A and B.
questions.question:
Consider the substrate 3,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol. It is subjected to two separate reactions:
Reaction 1: Treatment with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and heat to give major product A.
Reaction 2: Treatment with $\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}$ and pyridine to give major product B.
Identify the IUPAC names of the major products A and B.
questions.solution:
Reaction 1: 3,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol reacts with conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ upon heating. Protonation of the hydroxyl group followed by loss of water generates a secondary carbocation at C-2. A 1,2-methyl shift occurs to form a more stable tertiary carbocation at C-3. Subsequent loss of a proton yields the most substituted alkene, 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene, as the major product A (Saytzeff's rule).

Reaction 2: 3,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol reacts with $\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}$ and pyridine. The oxygen atom of the alcohol acts as a nucleophile and attacks the carbonyl carbon of acetyl chloride. The C-O bond of the alcohol is not broken, so no carbocation is formed and no skeletal rearrangement occurs. Pyridine acts as a base to remove the proton, yielding 3,3-dimethylbutan-2-yl acetate as product B.

Answer: A = 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene ; B = 3,3-dimethylbutan-2-yl acetate

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Benzene reacts with propene in the presence of $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ to give compound 'A'. 'A' undergoes oxidation with $\text{O}_2$ followed by acidic hydrolysis to yield 'B' and acetone. 'B' is treated with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ and $\text{CO}_2$ at 400 K and 4-7 atm pressure, followed by acidification to give 'C' as the major product. 'C' is then heated with acetic anhydride and a catalytic amount of conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to yield 'D'.

Identify the final product 'D'.
questions.question:
Benzene reacts with propene in the presence of $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ to give compound 'A'. 'A' undergoes oxidation with $\text{O}_2$ followed by acidic hydrolysis to yield 'B' and acetone. 'B' is treated with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ and $\text{CO}_2$ at 400 K and 4-7 atm pressure, followed by acidification to give 'C' as the major product. 'C' is then heated with acetic anhydride and a catalytic amount of conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to yield 'D'.

Identify the final product 'D'.
questions.solution:
Benzene undergoes Friedel-Crafts alkylation with propene in the presence of an acid catalyst ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$) to form isopropylbenzene, commonly known as cumene (Compound 'A').

Cumene is oxidized by air ($\text{O}_2$) to cumene hydroperoxide, which upon subsequent acidic hydrolysis yields phenol (Compound 'B') and acetone as a byproduct.

Phenol ('B') reacts with sodium hydroxide to form sodium phenoxide, which then undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution with $\text{CO}_2$ under high pressure and temperature (Kolbe's reaction). Acidification of the resulting salt yields 2-hydroxybenzoic acid, also known as salicylic acid (Compound 'C').

Salicylic acid ('C') contains both a phenolic $-\text{OH}$ group and a carboxylic acid $-\text{COOH}$ group. When treated with acetic anhydride in the presence of a catalytic amount of concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, the phenolic $-\text{OH}$ group undergoes acetylation. This esterification yields 2-acetoxybenzoic acid, which is commonly known as aspirin (Compound 'D').

Answer: 2-Acetoxybenzoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An unknown straight-chain diol $X$ ($C_4H_{10}O_2$) is heated with concentrated $H_2SO_4$ to yield a hydrocarbon $Y$. Reductive ozonolysis of $Y$ produces two moles of formaldehyde and one mole of glyoxal. The IUPAC name of diol $X$ is:
questions.question: An unknown straight-chain diol $X$ ($C_4H_{10}O_2$) is heated with concentrated $H_2SO_4$ to yield a hydrocarbon $Y$. Reductive ozonolysis of $Y$ produces two moles of formaldehyde and one mole of glyoxal. The IUPAC name of diol $X$ is:
questions.solution:
Reductive ozonolysis of hydrocarbon $Y$ yields two moles of formaldehyde ($HCHO$) and one mole of glyoxal ($OHC-CHO$).

Working backwards, the structure of $Y$ is obtained by joining the carbonyl carbons with double bonds:
$CH_2=O + O=CH-CH=O + O=CH_2 \rightarrow CH_2=CH-CH=CH_2$
Thus, $Y$ is 1,3-butadiene.

Diol $X$ is a straight-chain compound with the formula $C_4H_{10}O_2$ that undergoes dehydration to form 1,3-butadiene.

Let us examine the dehydration of the given straight-chain diols:
Butane-1,4-diol undergoes intramolecular dehydration to form tetrahydrofuran (a cyclic ether).
Butane-1,2-diol and Butane-2,3-diol undergo rearrangement to form butanone.
Butane-1,3-diol undergoes double elimination to form the conjugated diene, 1,3-butadiene.

Therefore, diol $X$ is Butane-1,3-diol.

Answer: Butane-1,3-diol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I : Ethanol has a significantly higher boiling point than its isomer dimethyl ether.
Statement II : Both ethanol and dimethyl ether react vigorously with potassium metal to liberate hydrogen gas.

In the light of the given statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I : Ethanol has a significantly higher boiling point than its isomer dimethyl ether.
Statement II : Both ethanol and dimethyl ether react vigorously with potassium metal to liberate hydrogen gas.

In the light of the given statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct because ethanol molecules are associated through strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding due to the presence of the -OH group. Dimethyl ether molecules cannot form intermolecular hydrogen bonds with each other. Thus, ethanol has a much higher boiling point.

Statement II is incorrect because ethanol contains an active (acidic) hydrogen and reacts with active metals like potassium to release hydrogen gas. Dimethyl ether lacks an active hydrogen and does not react with potassium metal.

Answer: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An unknown enol ether (X) undergoes mild acidic hydrolysis to yield two compounds, (Y) and (Z). Compound (Y) gives a positive Tollens' test but a negative iodoform test. Compound (Z) gives a negative Tollens' test but a positive iodoform test. Which of the following could be the structure of (X)?
questions.question: An unknown enol ether (X) undergoes mild acidic hydrolysis to yield two compounds, (Y) and (Z). Compound (Y) gives a positive Tollens' test but a negative iodoform test. Compound (Z) gives a negative Tollens' test but a positive iodoform test. Which of the following could be the structure of (X)?
questions.solution:
Mild acidic hydrolysis of an enol ether yields a carbonyl compound and an alcohol.

Compound (Y) gives a positive Tollens' test, so it must be an aldehyde. It gives a negative iodoform test, so it cannot be acetaldehyde ($CH_3CHO$). Thus, (Y) could be an aldehyde like propanal ($CH_3CH_2CHO$).

Compound (Z) gives a negative Tollens' test but a positive iodoform test. Since it is formed alongside a carbonyl compound, (Z) must be the alcohol product. Alcohols that give a positive iodoform test have the structure $CH_3-CH(OH)-R$. Ethanol ($CH_3CH_2OH$) is a primary alcohol that gives this test.

Let us evaluate the given options:
Option 1: $CH_3-CH=CH-O-CH_3$ hydrolyses to propanal and methanol. Methanol does not give the iodoform test.
Option 2: $CH_3-CH=CH-O-CH_2CH_3$ hydrolyses to propanal and ethanol. Propanal gives Tollens' but not iodoform. Ethanol gives iodoform but not Tollens'. This matches all conditions.
Option 3: $CH_2=C(CH_3)-O-CH_2CH_3$ hydrolyses to acetone and ethanol. Acetone does not give Tollens' test.
Option 4: $CH_2=CH-O-CH(CH_3)_2$ hydrolyses to acetaldehyde and isopropanol. Acetaldehyde gives both Tollens' and iodoform tests.

Therefore, the correct structure is $CH_3-CH=CH-O-CH_2CH_3$.

Answer: $CH_3-CH=CH-O-CH_2CH_3$

questions.q:
Consider the following three diols:
(I) Butane-1,4-diol
(II) 2,3-Dimethylbutane-2,3-diol
(III) Butane-1,3-diol

When each of these diols is heated separately with concentrated $H_2SO_4$, the major organic products formed are respectively:
questions.question:
Consider the following three diols:
(I) Butane-1,4-diol
(II) 2,3-Dimethylbutane-2,3-diol
(III) Butane-1,3-diol

When each of these diols is heated separately with concentrated $H_2SO_4$, the major organic products formed are respectively:
questions.solution:
The reaction of diols with concentrated $H_2SO_4$ and heat depends on the relative positions of the hydroxyl groups:

(I) Butane-1,4-diol: Protonation of one hydroxyl group followed by the loss of water and intramolecular attack by the other hydroxyl group leads to the formation of a stable five-membered cyclic ether. The major product is tetrahydrofuran.

(II) 2,3-Dimethylbutane-2,3-diol: This is a vicinal (1,2) diol. Under acidic conditions, it undergoes the pinacol-pinacolone rearrangement. Protonation and loss of water form a carbocation, followed by a methyl shift to generate a more stable resonance-stabilized carbocation, which loses a proton to form a ketone. The major product is 3,3-dimethylbutan-2-one (pinacolone).

(III) Butane-1,3-diol: Protonation and elimination of both hydroxyl groups occur to form a highly stable conjugated diene. The major product is 1,3-butadiene.

Thus, the products are Tetrahydrofuran, 3,3-Dimethylbutan-2-one, and 1,3-Butadiene respectively.

Answer: (I) Tetrahydrofuran, (II) 3,3-Dimethylbutan-2-one, (III) 1,3-Butadiene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When optically active 2-chloro-3-methylhexane is treated with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$, what is the structure and stereochemical nature of the major product formed?
questions.question: When optically active 2-chloro-3-methylhexane is treated with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$, what is the structure and stereochemical nature of the major product formed?
questions.solution:
The reaction of a secondary alkyl halide in a polar protic solvent (aqueous $\text{NaOH}$) proceeds via an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ mechanism.

First, ionization of optically active 2-chloro-3-methylhexane forms a secondary carbocation at C2:
$\text{CH}_3\text{-CH(Cl)-CH(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{-CH}^+\text{-CH(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_3$

Next, a 1,2-hydride shift from the adjacent tertiary C3 carbon occurs to generate a more stable tertiary carbocation at C3:
$\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}^+\text{-CH(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-C}^+\text{(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_3$

The tertiary carbocation intermediate is $\text{sp}^2$ hybridized and planar. The nucleophile ($\text{OH}^-$ or $\text{H}_2\text{O}$) can attack the empty p-orbital from either face with equal probability.

The attack yields 3-methylhexan-3-ol. Since the C3 carbon in the product is bonded to four different groups (methyl, ethyl, propyl, and hydroxyl), it is a chiral center. The equal probability of attack from both faces results in a 50:50 mixture of enantiomers, which is a racemic mixture.

Answer: A racemic mixture of 3-methylhexan-3-ol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When 1-methylcyclopentanol is heated with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, it undergoes dehydration to give a major product P. The compound P is then treated with a cold, dilute aqueous solution of $\text{KMnO}_4$ to yield the major product Q. The product Q is:
questions.question: When 1-methylcyclopentanol is heated with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, it undergoes dehydration to give a major product P. The compound P is then treated with a cold, dilute aqueous solution of $\text{KMnO}_4$ to yield the major product Q. The product Q is:
questions.solution:
Dehydration of 1-methylcyclopentanol with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ follows Saytzeff's rule, yielding the more substituted alkene as the major product. Thus, the major product P is 1-methylcyclopentene.

Treatment of 1-methylcyclopentene with cold, dilute aqueous $\text{KMnO}_4$ (Baeyer's reagent) brings about the syn-addition of two hydroxyl groups across the double bond.

Because the addition is syn, the two -OH groups attach to the same face of the cyclopentane ring.

This stereospecific reaction produces cis-1-methylcyclopentane-1,2-diol as the major product Q.

Answer: cis-1-Methylcyclopentane-1,2-diol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following two-step reaction sequences will yield 2-chloro-4-nitroanisole as the major product starting from anisole?
questions.question: Which of the following two-step reaction sequences will yield 2-chloro-4-nitroanisole as the major product starting from anisole?
questions.solution:
To synthesize 2-chloro-4-nitroanisole as the major product, we must consider the directing effects of the intermediate formed after the first step.

If chlorination is performed first: Anisole reacts with $\text{Cl}_2 / \text{FeCl}_3$ to give 4-chloroanisole as the major product (due to less steric hindrance at the para position). Subsequent nitration of 4-chloroanisole is controlled by the strongly activating $-\text{OCH}_3$ group, which directs the incoming $\text{NO}_2^+$ to its ortho position, yielding 4-chloro-2-nitroanisole. This is not the desired product.

If nitration is performed first: Anisole reacts with $\text{HNO}_3 / \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to give 4-nitroanisole as the major product. Subsequent chlorination of 4-nitroanisole involves synergistic directing effects. The $-\text{OCH}_3$ group (ortho/para directing) directs the incoming $\text{Cl}^+$ to its ortho position, and the $-\text{NO}_2$ group (meta directing) also directs it to the same position. Using 1 equivalent of $\text{Cl}_2 / \text{FeCl}_3$ yields the desired 2-chloro-4-nitroanisole as the major product.

Excess $\text{Cl}_2$ would lead to 2,6-dichloro-4-nitroanisole. Thus, the correct sequence is nitration followed by mono-chlorination.

Answer: (i) $\text{HNO}_3, \text{ H}_2\text{SO}_4$ followed by (ii) $\text{Cl}_2, \text{ FeCl}_3$ (1 eq)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following sequence of reactions:

Acetaldehyde $\xrightarrow{\text{HCN}}$ A $\xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+}$ B

B $\xrightarrow{\text{Acetone, H}^+}$ C (Major Product)

The IUPAC name of the major product C is:
questions.question:
Consider the following sequence of reactions:

Acetaldehyde $\xrightarrow{\text{HCN}}$ A $\xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+}$ B

B $\xrightarrow{\text{Acetone, H}^+}$ C (Major Product)

The IUPAC name of the major product C is:
questions.solution:
Acetaldehyde reacts with HCN to undergo nucleophilic addition, forming acetaldehyde cyanohydrin (A).
$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CN}$

Acidic hydrolysis of the nitrile group in A yields lactic acid (2-hydroxypropanoic acid), which is B.
$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CN} + \text{H}_3\text{O}^+ \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{COOH} + \text{NH}_4^+$

Lactic acid (B) reacts with acetone in the presence of an acid catalyst. The hydroxyl group of lactic acid attacks the carbonyl carbon of acetone to form a hemiketal. Subsequently, intramolecular esterification occurs between the carboxylic acid group and the newly formed hemiketal hydroxyl group, eliminating a water molecule.
This forms a 5-membered cyclic acetal-lactone ring.
The ring contains an -O-C(CH$_3$)$_2$-O- linkage from the acetone part and a -CH(CH$_3$)-C(=O)- part from the lactic acid.
Numbering the heterocycle starting from the acetal oxygen as 1, the acetal carbon as 2, the ester oxygen as 3, the carbonyl carbon as 4, and the chiral carbon as 5, we get 1,3-dioxolan-4-one.
The substituents are two methyl groups at position 2 and one methyl group at position 5.
Thus, the IUPAC name of product C is 2,2,5-trimethyl-1,3-dioxolan-4-one.

Answer: 2,2,5-trimethyl-1,3-dioxolan-4-one

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
An optically active secondary alcohol X ($\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}$) undergoes acid-catalyzed dehydration to give alkene Y as the major product. Ozonolysis of Y yields a mixture of acetone and acetaldehyde. Reaction of X with acetyl chloride in the presence of pyridine gives an ester Z.
Identify the IUPAC names of X, Y, and Z.
questions.question:
An optically active secondary alcohol X ($\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}$) undergoes acid-catalyzed dehydration to give alkene Y as the major product. Ozonolysis of Y yields a mixture of acetone and acetaldehyde. Reaction of X with acetyl chloride in the presence of pyridine gives an ester Z.
Identify the IUPAC names of X, Y, and Z.
options: X = pentan-2-ol ; Y = pent-2-ene ; Z = pentan-2-yl acetate
questions.solution:
Ozonolysis of alkene Y yields acetone ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$) and acetaldehyde ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$). Working backwards, joining the carbonyl carbons with a double bond gives Y as 2-methylbut-2-ene ($\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3$).

Alcohol X ($\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}$) dehydrates to give Y as the major product. The possible alcohols are 2-methylbutan-2-ol and 3-methylbutan-2-ol. Since X is an optically active secondary alcohol, it must be the chiral 3-methylbutan-2-ol (which has a chiral center at C-2). Dehydration of 3-methylbutan-2-ol involves a secondary carbocation that undergoes a 1,2-hydride shift to form a tertiary carbocation, leading to Y.

Reaction of X with acetyl chloride and pyridine is an esterification. The C-O bond of the alcohol remains intact, so no rearrangement of the carbon skeleton occurs. Thus, X directly forms the ester Z, which is 3-methylbutan-2-yl acetate.

Answer: X = 3-methylbutan-2-ol ; Y = 2-methylbut-2-ene ; Z = 3-methylbutan-2-yl acetate
