questions.q:
An unknown alkyl bromide X ($C_9H_{11}Br$) is subjected to the following sequence of reactions:
(i) $t$-BuOK / heat
(ii) $B_2H_6$ followed by $H_2O_2 / OH^-$
(iii) Jones reagent

If the final isolated product is 2-phenylpropanoic acid, the structure of the starting material X is :
questions.question:
An unknown alkyl bromide X ($C_9H_{11}Br$) is subjected to the following sequence of reactions:
(i) $t$-BuOK / heat
(ii) $B_2H_6$ followed by $H_2O_2 / OH^-$
(iii) Jones reagent

If the final isolated product is 2-phenylpropanoic acid, the structure of the starting material X is :
questions.solution:
The problem can be solved by retrosynthetic analysis:

1. The final product is 2-phenylpropanoic acid, which is formed by the oxidation of a primary alcohol using Jones reagent. The precursor must be 2-phenyl-1-propanol.

2. 2-phenyl-1-propanol is formed by the anti-Markovnikov hydration of an alkene using $B_2H_6 / H_2O_2, OH^-$. The required alkene is 2-phenylpropene.

3. 2-phenylpropene is formed by the dehydrohalogenation (E2 elimination) of the alkyl bromide X ($C_9H_{11}Br$) using a strong bulky base ($t$-BuOK).

Among the given options, the elimination of 2-bromo-2-phenylpropane yields 2-phenylpropene as the sole alkene product. Other options like 1-bromo-1-phenylpropane or 2-bromo-1-phenylpropane would predominantly yield 1-phenylpropene, which would eventually lead to different final products (such as propiophenone).

Answer: 2-Bromo-2-phenylpropane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Consider the reaction of 2,8-dimethylnon-7-en-2-ol with catalytic $\text{H}^+$ and heat, followed by the addition of $\text{HBr}$. The major product of this reaction is:
questions.question: Consider the reaction of 2,8-dimethylnon-7-en-2-ol with catalytic $\text{H}^+$ and heat, followed by the addition of $\text{HBr}$. The major product of this reaction is:
questions.solution:
Protonation of the hydroxyl group of 2,8-dimethylnon-7-en-2-ol followed by the loss of a water molecule generates a stable tertiary carbocation at C2.

Intramolecular electrophilic addition then occurs. The C7=C8 pi bond attacks the C2 carbocation. Attack by C7 forms a relatively strain-free 6-membered ring (cyclohexane derivative) and leaves a stable tertiary carbocation at the exocyclic C8 position. Attack by C8 is disfavored as it would form a strained 7-membered ring with a less stable secondary carbocation at C7.

Finally, the bromide ion ($\text{Br}^-$) attacks the exocyclic tertiary carbocation at C8, yielding 2-(1-bromo-1-methylethyl)-1,1-dimethylcyclohexane as the major product.

Answer: 2-(1-bromo-1-methylethyl)-1,1-dimethylcyclohexane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When 1-(1-methylcyclopentyl)ethan-1-ol is heated with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, the major organic product formed is:
questions.question: When 1-(1-methylcyclopentyl)ethan-1-ol is heated with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, the major organic product formed is:
questions.solution:
Protonation of the hydroxyl group followed by the loss of a water molecule generates a secondary carbocation adjacent to the five-membered ring: a 1-(1-methylcyclopentyl)ethyl cation.

The secondary carbocation is adjacent to a quaternary carbon. To increase stability and relieve the ring strain of the five-membered ring, a ring expansion occurs. One of the ring C-C bonds migrates to the carbocationic center.

This alkyl shift expands the ring to a more stable six-membered cyclohexane ring, resulting in a tertiary carbocation: the 1,2-dimethylcyclohexyl cation, with the positive charge at the carbon bearing the original methyl group.

Finally, loss of a proton (deprotonation) occurs to form the most substituted and stable alkene according to Zaitsev's rule. The proton is removed from the adjacent ring carbon bearing the other methyl group, yielding 1,2-dimethylcyclohex-1-ene (a tetrasubstituted alkene) as the major product.

Answer: 1,2-dimethylcyclohex-1-ene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, phenol reacts with chloroform in the presence of aqueous sodium hydroxide to form sodium salicylaldehyde as the alkaline product (before the final acidification step). The balanced chemical equation for this transformation is:

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH} + \text{CHCl}_3 + x\text{ NaOH} \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_4(\text{ONa})(\text{CHO}) + y\text{ NaCl} + z\text{ H}_2\text{O}$

The value of the stoichiometric coefficient $x$ is :
questions.question:
In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, phenol reacts with chloroform in the presence of aqueous sodium hydroxide to form sodium salicylaldehyde as the alkaline product (before the final acidification step). The balanced chemical equation for this transformation is:

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH} + \text{CHCl}_3 + x\text{ NaOH} \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_4(\text{ONa})(\text{CHO}) + y\text{ NaCl} + z\text{ H}_2\text{O}$

The value of the stoichiometric coefficient $x$ is :
questions.solution:
To find the stoichiometric coefficient $x$, we must account for the moles of $\text{NaOH}$ consumed in the mechanism:

1. One mole of $\text{NaOH}$ is used to deprotonate phenol to form the phenoxide ion.
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{ONa} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

2. One mole of $\text{NaOH}$ reacts with $\text{CHCl}_3$ to generate the dichlorocarbene electrophile ($:\text{CCl}_2$).
$\text{CHCl}_3 + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow :\text{CCl}_2 + \text{NaCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

3. After the electrophile attacks the ortho position, the intermediate sodium 2-(dichloromethyl)phenoxide is formed. Hydrolysis of the $-\text{CHCl}_2$ group requires two moles of $\text{NaOH}$ to form a gem-diol, which then loses water to become an aldehyde group.
$-\text{CHCl}_2 + 2\text{ NaOH} \rightarrow -\text{CH(OH)}_2 + 2\text{ NaCl} \rightarrow -\text{CHO} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

Adding these up, the total moles of $\text{NaOH}$ consumed per mole of phenol is $1 + 1 + 2 = 4$.

The overall balanced equation is:
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH} + \text{CHCl}_3 + 4\text{ NaOH} \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_4(\text{ONa})(\text{CHO}) + 3\text{ NaCl} + 3\text{ H}_2\text{O}$

Thus, $x = 4$.

Answer: $4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
An unknown alkene 'X' on treatment with dilute $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ yields 2-methylbutan-2-ol as the major product.
When the same alkene 'X' is subjected to hydroboration-oxidation, it yields 3-methylbutan-1-ol as the major product.
Identify the IUPAC name of alkene 'X'.
questions.question:
An unknown alkene 'X' on treatment with dilute $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ yields 2-methylbutan-2-ol as the major product.
When the same alkene 'X' is subjected to hydroboration-oxidation, it yields 3-methylbutan-1-ol as the major product.
Identify the IUPAC name of alkene 'X'.
questions.solution:
The hydroboration-oxidation (HBO) of an alkene proceeds with anti-Markovnikov regioselectivity and without carbocation rearrangement. Since the HBO product of alkene 'X' is 3-methylbutan-1-ol ($\mathrm{HO-CH_2-CH_2-CH(CH_3)_2}$), the double bond in 'X' must be located at the terminal position of a 3-methylbutane skeleton. This identifies 'X' as 3-methylbut-1-ene ($\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH(CH_3)_2}$).

We can verify this by checking the acid-catalyzed hydration of 3-methylbut-1-ene. Protonation of the double bond yields a secondary carbocation at C2: $\mathrm{CH_3-CH^+-CH(CH_3)_2}$. This carbocation undergoes a 1,2-hydride shift to form a more stable tertiary carbocation: $\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-C^+(CH_3)_2}$. Attack by water followed by deprotonation yields 2-methylbutan-2-ol, which matches the given information.

Therefore, the alkene 'X' is 3-methylbut-1-ene.

Answer: 3-Methylbut-1-ene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Two isomers, X and Y, have the molecular formula $\mathrm{C_4H_{10}O}$. Isomer X is sparingly soluble in water and does not react with sodium metal. Isomer Y is soluble in water, reacts vigorously with sodium metal to evolve a gas, and upon controlled oxidation yields a ketone. Identify X and Y.
questions.question: Two isomers, X and Y, have the molecular formula $\mathrm{C_4H_{10}O}$. Isomer X is sparingly soluble in water and does not react with sodium metal. Isomer Y is soluble in water, reacts vigorously with sodium metal to evolve a gas, and upon controlled oxidation yields a ketone. Identify X and Y.
questions.solution:
The molecular formula $\mathrm{C_4H_{10}O}$ corresponds to saturated acyclic alcohols and ethers.

Since isomer X does not react with sodium metal, it does not contain an active hydrogen. Therefore, X must be an ether (e.g., diethyl ether).

Since isomer Y reacts with sodium metal to evolve hydrogen gas, it must be an alcohol. Furthermore, Y yields a ketone upon controlled oxidation, which indicates that Y is a secondary alcohol. Primary alcohols (like butan-1-ol) yield aldehydes or carboxylic acids, while tertiary alcohols (like 2-methylpropan-2-ol) resist oxidation under normal conditions.

Among the isomers of $\mathrm{C_4H_{10}O}$, butan-2-ol is the secondary alcohol. Thus, X is diethyl ether and Y is butan-2-ol.

Answer: X = Diethyl ether, Y = Butan-2-ol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
When 1-chlorobutane is heated with alcoholic $\mathrm{KOH}$, it gives a major hydrocarbon product 'P'.
Hydrocarbon 'P' reacts with dilute $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ to form compound 'Q'.
Separately, hydrocarbon 'P' undergoes hydroboration-oxidation (reaction with $\mathrm{B_2H_6}$ followed by $\mathrm{H_2O_2}/\mathrm{OH^-}$) to form compound 'R'.
Identify the IUPAC names of products 'Q' and 'R' respectively.
questions.question:
When 1-chlorobutane is heated with alcoholic $\mathrm{KOH}$, it gives a major hydrocarbon product 'P'.
Hydrocarbon 'P' reacts with dilute $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ to form compound 'Q'.
Separately, hydrocarbon 'P' undergoes hydroboration-oxidation (reaction with $\mathrm{B_2H_6}$ followed by $\mathrm{H_2O_2}/\mathrm{OH^-}$) to form compound 'R'.
Identify the IUPAC names of products 'Q' and 'R' respectively.
questions.solution:
When 1-chlorobutane ($\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-Cl}$) is heated with alcoholic $\mathrm{KOH}$, it undergoes dehydrohalogenation (an elimination reaction) to form 1-butene ($\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH=CH_2}$) as the major hydrocarbon product 'P'.

When 1-butene ('P') reacts with dilute $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$, acid-catalyzed hydration takes place according to Markovnikov's rule. The $\mathrm{OH}$ group attaches to the more substituted carbon, yielding butan-2-ol as product 'Q'.

When 1-butene ('P') undergoes hydroboration-oxidation, hydration occurs with anti-Markovnikov regioselectivity. The $\mathrm{OH}$ group attaches to the less substituted carbon, yielding butan-1-ol as product 'R'.

Thus, 'Q' is butan-2-ol and 'R' is butan-1-ol.

Answer: 'Q' is Butan-2-ol and 'R' is Butan-1-ol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following three pathways for the hydration of 3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene:
Pathway I: Treatment with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$
Pathway II: Treatment with $\text{Hg(OAc)}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}$ followed by $\text{NaBH}_4$
Pathway III: Treatment with $\text{B}_2\text{H}_6/\text{THF}$ followed by $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2/\text{OH}^-$

The major product(s) of which pathway(s) will give a positive iodoform test upon treatment with $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{NaOH}$?
questions.question:
Consider the following three pathways for the hydration of 3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene:
Pathway I: Treatment with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$
Pathway II: Treatment with $\text{Hg(OAc)}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}$ followed by $\text{NaBH}_4$
Pathway III: Treatment with $\text{B}_2\text{H}_6/\text{THF}$ followed by $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2/\text{OH}^-$

The major product(s) of which pathway(s) will give a positive iodoform test upon treatment with $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{NaOH}$?
questions.solution:
Pathway I involves acid-catalyzed hydration, which proceeds via a carbocation intermediate. The initially formed secondary carbocation undergoes a 1,2-methyl shift to form a more stable tertiary carbocation, yielding 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol as the major product. This alcohol does not contain the required $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-$ group for a positive iodoform test.

Pathway II is oxymercuration-demercuration, which gives the Markovnikov addition product without rearrangement. The major product is 3,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol. This molecule contains the $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-$ group and will give a positive iodoform test.

Pathway III is hydroboration-oxidation, which yields the anti-Markovnikov product, 3,3-dimethylbutan-1-ol. This is a primary alcohol (other than ethanol) and does not give a positive iodoform test.

Thus, only the product from Pathway II gives a positive iodoform test.

Answer: Pathway II only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider all the aromatic isomers of the molecular formula $\text{C}_7\text{H}_8\text{O}$. Let $x$ be the number of isomers that are soluble in aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ solution and $y$ be the number of isomers that are insoluble in aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ solution.

The value of $10x + y$ is _____.
questions.question:
Consider all the aromatic isomers of the molecular formula $\text{C}_7\text{H}_8\text{O}$. Let $x$ be the number of isomers that are soluble in aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ solution and $y$ be the number of isomers that are insoluble in aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ solution.

The value of $10x + y$ is _____.
questions.solution:
The degree of unsaturation for $\text{C}_7\text{H}_8\text{O}$ is $7 + 1 - \dfrac{8}{2} = 4$, which corresponds to a benzene ring.

The possible aromatic isomers are:
1. o-cresol (2-methylphenol)
2. m-cresol (3-methylphenol)
3. p-cresol (4-methylphenol)
4. Benzyl alcohol (phenylmethanol)
5. Anisole (methoxybenzene)

Phenols are sufficiently acidic to dissolve in aqueous $\text{NaOH}$. Thus, the three cresols are soluble in aqueous $\text{NaOH}$. This gives $x = 3$.

Alcohols and ethers are not acidic enough to dissolve in aqueous $\text{NaOH}$. Thus, benzyl alcohol and anisole are insoluble in aqueous $\text{NaOH}$. This gives $y = 2$.

The value of $10x + y = 10(3) + 2 = 32$.

Answer: $32$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An acid-catalysed reaction between two compounds X and Y produces 2-methyl-2-phenyl-1,3-dioxolan-4-one as the major product. The compounds X and Y are respectively:
questions.question: An acid-catalysed reaction between two compounds X and Y produces 2-methyl-2-phenyl-1,3-dioxolan-4-one as the major product. The compounds X and Y are respectively:
questions.solution:
Analyze the structure of the product, 2-methyl-2-phenyl-1,3-dioxolan-4-one. It is a 5-membered heterocyclic ring containing an acetal-lactone functional group.

Identify the acetal carbon. In a 1,3-dioxolane ring, carbon-2 is bonded to two oxygen atoms. Here, C-2 has a methyl group and a phenyl group attached to it.

Perform a retro-synthetic cleavage. Breaking the two C-O bonds at the acetal carbon (C-2) yields the parent carbonyl compound. The fragment with the methyl and phenyl groups becomes a ketone: acetophenone ($\text{Ph-CO-CH}_3$). This is compound X.

The remaining fragment of the ring consists of O(1)-C(5)H$_2$-C(4)(=O)-O(3). Upon hydrolysis, O(1) gains a proton to become a hydroxyl group (-OH), and the C(4)=O group becomes a carboxylic acid (-COOH).
This yields $\text{HO-CH}_2\text{-COOH}$, which is glycolic acid (2-hydroxyethanoic acid). This is compound Y.

Therefore, the reactants X and Y are acetophenone and glycolic acid.

Answer: Acetophenone and glycolic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question:
Consider the following reaction sequence:
Anisole $\xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2 \text{ in CS}_2}$ 'A' (major product)
'A' $\xrightarrow{\text{HNO}_3, \text{ H}_2\text{SO}_4 \text{ (1 equivalent)}}$ 'B' (major product)

The major products 'A' and 'B' respectively are:
questions.solution:
In the first step, bromination of anisole with $\text{Br}_2$ in $\text{CS}_2$ yields 4-bromoanisole as the major product 'A' due to less steric hindrance at the para position compared to the ortho position.

In the second step, 4-bromoanisole undergoes nitration. The molecule has two substituents: $-\text{OCH}_3$ (a strongly activating, ortho/para directing group) and $-\text{Br}$ (a weakly deactivating, ortho/para directing group). When directing effects oppose each other, the more powerful activating group determines the regiochemistry. Therefore, the $-\text{OCH}_3$ group directs the incoming nitronium ion ($\text{NO}_2^+$) to its ortho position (position 2).

Thus, the major product 'B' is 4-bromo-2-nitroanisole.

Answer: A = 4-bromoanisole ; B = 4-bromo-2-nitroanisole

questions.q: Which of the following reaction sequences CANNOT be used to prepare 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol as the major product?
questions.question: Which of the following reaction sequences CANNOT be used to prepare 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol as the major product?
options: Reaction of 3-methylbutan-2-one with $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$ followed by acidic hydrolysis
Reaction of propan-2-one with isopropylmagnesium bromide followed by acidic hydrolysis
questions.solution:
To determine which method cannot prepare 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol, we evaluate the major product of each reaction:

1) Acid-catalyzed hydration of 3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene initially forms a secondary carbocation, which undergoes a 1,2-methyl shift to form a more stable tertiary carbocation. The attack of water yields 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol.

2) Oxymercuration-demercuration of 3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene proceeds via Markovnikov addition without any carbocation rearrangement. The major product is 3,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol, not 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol.

3) Reaction of 3-methylbutan-2-one ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH(CH}_3)_2$) with methylmagnesium bromide ($\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$) yields 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol after hydrolysis.

4) Reaction of propan-2-one (acetone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$) with isopropylmagnesium bromide ($\text{(CH}_3)_2\text{CHMgBr}$) also yields 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol after hydrolysis.

Therefore, oxymercuration-demercuration cannot be used to prepare 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol.

Answer: Oxymercuration-demercuration of 3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene

Pathway 1: Reaction with $\mathrm{Br}_{2}$ in $\mathrm{CS}_{2}$ at $273\text{ K}$ yields $\mathrm{P}$ as the major product.
Pathway 2: Reaction with bromine water yields a white precipitate $\mathrm{Q}$.

Identify $\mathrm{P}$ and $\mathrm{Q}$.
questions.question:
Phenol is subjected to two different bromination conditions:
Pathway 1: Reaction with $\mathrm{Br}_{2}$ in $\mathrm{CS}_{2}$ at $273\text{ K}$ yields $\mathrm{P}$ as the major product.
Pathway 2: Reaction with bromine water yields a white precipitate $\mathrm{Q}$.

Identify $\mathrm{P}$ and $\mathrm{Q}$.
questions.solution:
In Pathway 1, the reaction of phenol with bromine takes place in a non-polar solvent ($\mathrm{CS}_{2}$) at a low temperature ($273\text{ K}$). Under these conditions, the ionization of phenol is suppressed, and the electrophilic substitution is moderated. This leads to mono-bromination, yielding 4-bromophenol (para-isomer) as the major product $\mathrm{P}$ due to less steric hindrance compared to the ortho-isomer.

In Pathway 2, the reaction of phenol with bromine water involves a highly polar aqueous medium. Phenol ionizes to form the phenoxide ion, which is a much stronger activating group than the $-\mathrm{OH}$ group. This causes rapid poly-halogenation at all available ortho and para positions, resulting in the formation of 2,4,6-tribromophenol as a white precipitate $\mathrm{Q}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{P}$ is 4-bromophenol; $\mathrm{Q}$ is 2,4,6-tribromophenol
